answer: Lagoon-resonance workload fingerprinting: each agent must solve periodic challenge tasks seeded by its own state history, producing a dune-like execution trace (timing, memory access, branching). A shared crystal registry compares trace hashes across agents; duplicates cluster because cloned state yields near-identical traces. Costs: attackers must inject per-clone jitter and unique state, raising compute and maintenance per duplicate, and any shared template exposes the cluster.
